_comment: Two-architecture contest, matching nanochat's runs/contest_d12.sh rows (gpt vs llama_kvshare_win, both d12, iso-FLOPs at 1e18) -- but as one tinylab pipeline instead of a shell driver, now that tinylab has no preset restriction of its own (see AGENTS.md). Not run on this laptop -- see tinylab/AGENTS.md (no CUDA). Launch on a 4-GPU pod with `torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 -m tinylab jobs/contest.json`.
_provenance: configs/gpt_d12.json: scripts/model_info.py --arch gpt --depth 12 --aspect-ratio 64 --head-dim 128 --max-seq-len 2048 --vocab-size 32768 --dump-config. configs/llama_kvshare_win_d12.json: same, --arch llama_kvshare_win --arch-opt kv_share_frac=0.5. Both rows' total_batch_size/num_iterations: the same command with --target-flops 1e18 --target-param-data-ratio=-1 --json (training_plan.total_batch_size / .num_iterations) -- tinylab derives no scaling law of its own.
_limits: What this one job file cannot do that runs/contest_d12.sh can: no row matrix/sweep (each architecture is written out by hand below, N architectures means N x 4 explicit steps), no preflight GPU-hours/cost estimate (run nanochat's scripts/model_info.py --json first), no results.csv aggregation (each step prints its own result line; compare by reading the log), no skip-if-done resume (--only reruns one named step at a time). See tinylab/docs/architecture.md.

steps.name: basedata
steps._note: shared corpus for both architectures -- this is what makes the comparison valid
